name: Hullbreak CORROSION Tour Tee
description:
Black heavyweight cotton-poly with a bleach-damaged front print — the band name HULLBREAK in corroded industrial lettering above a cracked turbine graphic, the word CORROSION in smaller type below, and the tour dates printed down the left sleeve: seventeen Shelf-level venues across the Great Lakes corridor, year 2198. The back has a full cityscape of the lower Meridian 88 waterfront rendered in a single-color white screenprint, partially cracked from washing.

Hullbreak is a post-industrial noise band that has never played above Tier 2. Their shows are loud, dangerous, and technically unpermitted in most of the venues they play anyway. This shirt is a badge of having been there — in the pit, in the dark, in the noise. Counterfeits exist but the real ones have a small stamped number on the interior tag (1 through 500, the original run).
what_it_says: I was there. I survived it. I liked it.
story_hooks: The shirt's tour dates include a venue that burned down the night of the show — anyone wearing one of the originals was in that building.
A Spire music collector is quietly paying premium prices for authenticated originals; someone on the Shelf has six of them and doesn't know what they're worth.
One of the numbered shirts (No. 7) was worn by someone who disappeared after the final tour date — the shirt has become an urban legend in certain Shelf circles.
